claims.text: Graph Neural Networks trained on high-entropy-alloy datasets can accurately predict phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach can identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity for thermal-insulation applications.
High-entropy alloys possess structural complexity that is relevant to phonon thermal conductivity.
GNNs can learn representations that navigate the structural complexity of high-entropy alloys.
Patterns in high-entropy-alloy data correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Learning these patterns enables GNNs to make accurate thermal-conductivity predictions.
The GNN approach could reduce prediction error by 20–30% relative to current prediction methods.
Current methods for predicting phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys are inaccurate.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys and thermal-insulation applications.
The approach may not generalize to other material classes or applications.
Out-of-sample MAE and R-squared can be used to compare the GNN with current prediction methods.
Failure to improve both MAE and R-squared over current prediction methods would falsify the hypothesis.
